text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnian presidency agrees formation of a permanent committee for military matters during visit of U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright. The committee, comprised of members from Moslem, Croat and Serb communities, is to oversee implementation of the arms agreement and defuse possible tensions.

- Bosnian Foreign Minister Jadranko Prlic says he reached an agreement on the opening of eight road and four rail crossings with his Croatian counterpart Mate Granic. The border crossings could be open within a few weeks, he says.

- Twenty private banks are registered in the country's Moslem-Croat federation, many of them opened in the past two years, according to government records. A relatively small amount of capital is required to set up a bank.

- Statements about Bosnia from Contact Group meeting in Sintra, Portugal, sounded nice but even after the new U.S. diplomatic show in Bosnia and neighbouring countries, it still remains unclear how to achieve these goals, commentary says.
- If people are not certain that the war is really over, then it is not possible to build democracy here, says Michael Steiner, deputy High representative to Bosnia.
- The first private medical clinic in Bosnia opened in Sarajevo. The cost of medical services will be less than in foreign medical centres. -- Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-384
